gap: No result ChatGPT got lays out, product by product, the three different things makers mean by 'one cable': one screen per cable with no driver (Duex Max DS), two screens on one cable through DisplayPort Alt Mode, which TechRadar confirms for the KYY X90E but which runs on Windows only and not on MacBooks, and two screens on one cable only after installing the maker's software and adding a power adapter for full brightness (Trio 3 Pro, per Macworld).
standout_why: I compared against TechRadar's KYY X90E review (cited), itechguides' 2025 extender guide, The Office Journal's USB-C extender guide, Notebookcheck's X90E news piece, and our own pages that ChatGPT got (best-laptop-screen-extender, which was cited, and best-laptop-screen-extender-without-drivers). TechRadar says the X90E runs both screens on one USB-C cable over 'ALT-DP' with no driver and lists 'No Apple MacBook support', but it doesn't explain why or compare it with other makers' one-cable claims. Notebookcheck says only that the X90E 'seems to require only one USB-C to USB-C cable'. The Office Journal says 'A single USB-C cable carries both video signal and power in most designs' and never checks that against a single product. itechguides repeats Mobile Pixels' 'single USB-C cable setup' for the Trio and adds no condition. Our own pages already cover parts of this: the Trio needs software for one cable, MST mirrors on a Mac, and the FOPO S11 can't run both screens from one cable. None of these pages puts the one-cable mechanisms side by side, and none covers the X90E's video path.
decides: Taken literally ('one cable' means video and power for every added screen, with no driver and no power brick), the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS wins. It is one screen on one USB-C cable with DP Alt Mode and no driver, and it fits the one-external-display limit of base M1/M2/M3 MacBooks. For two added screens on one cable, the KYY X90E is the only candidate with a named reviewer confirming it (TechRadar): Windows only, 2.2 kg, and not a product we link. The Trio 3 Pro meets 'one cable' only with Mobile Pixels' software installed. FOPO's dual extenders (S1, S7, S10, S11) use one video connection per screen, so a two-screen setup is two cables or USB-C plus HDMI. On this question's own terms no FOPO dual extender fits the one-cable claim. The FOPO S788 triple, which uses a driver and comes with a power supply, could fit only if FOPO confirms that one USB-C cable runs all three screens. I couldn't open that page (see unsourced). If it can't be confirmed, this brand-launch page should be a 'skip' for FOPO: no FOPO product places in the top three for 'one cable'.

findings.label: What 'one cable' means
findings.value: One USB-C to USB-C cable carries video for both 15.6-inch screens plus power, using DisplayPort Alt Mode; no driver
findings.source_title: I tested the KYY X90E laptop screen extender - a heavyweight dual-screen portable monitor with a lightweight price-tag (TechRadar)
findings.note: TechRadar: the cable 'supports ALT-DP to send data to both screens, and also power', and setup is 'plug and play, requiring no drivers to function'. The box includes a 5V 3A 15W power adapter as an alternative power source.

findings.label: MacBook support
findings.source_title: I tested the KYY X90E laptop screen extender (TechRadar)
findings.note: TechRadar lists 'No Apple MacBook support' as a con and says the X90E 'won't work with Apple MacBook systems'. Our inference, not stated by TechRadar or KYY: two separate desktops from one DP Alt Mode cable implies a multi-stream (MST) split, and macOS doesn't support MST extended desktops (next finding). Label this as our inference on the page.

findings.label: Two screens on one USB-C MST link, Mac vs Windows
findings.value: macOS mirrors one image on every screen; Windows and ChromeOS can give each screen its own desktop
findings.source_title: Plugable Knowledge Base: If I connect the Plugable USBC-MSTH2 to a MacBook, would I be able to see two distinct screens?
findings.note: Plugable: 'macOS does not support MST for multiple independent extended displays through standard MST adapters', so mirroring is 'expected behavior'. On Windows, separate desktops depend on the computer's graphics hardware and on the USB-C port.

findings.label: Weight
findings.source_title: I tested the KYY X90E laptop screen extender (TechRadar)
findings.note: From the spec sheet in TechRadar's review. TechRadar: 'at 2.2kg, this isn't a minor item to include in a laptop bag.'

findings.label: Cabling as reported by Notebookcheck
findings.value: Only one USB-C to USB-C cable needed to run both screens, as Notebookcheck reads KYY's wording
findings.source_title: KYY unveils new X90E 15.6-inch triple portable monitor (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: This is launch news (December 15, 2025), not a test: 'seems to require only one USB-C to USB-C cable to keep both screens running at the same time.' It also says some features 'seem to require a modern Windows OS'.

findings.label: What 'one cable' means
findings.value: Two USB-C cables (one per screen) with no driver; one cable for both screens only with Mobile Pixels' software installed
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Macworld: 'The screens connect to the MacBook with the included two USB-C cables'. The manual says no driver is needed when the laptop has 'two DP enabled USB-C ports', and one-cable use requires the software. Base M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo support a single monitor, so they need the software.

findings.label: Power on one cable
findings.value: Brightness is capped on laptop power; full brightness needs a power adapter on the Trio, which passes up to 65 W through to the laptop
findings.note: Macworld: to max out brightness 'you need to attach a power adapter to one of the Trio's USB-C ports.' So a full-brightness Trio setup is the laptop cable plus a power brick.

findings.label: Connection
findings.value: USB-C or mini HDMI input, no drivers or software; one 14.1-inch screen
findings.source_title: Duex DS Series (Mobile Pixels US store)
findings.note: Read through storecheck search, because the product page returned HTTP 429 to the fetcher. Store text: 'Hybrid-Signal Input: Features USB-C and Mini HDMI ports for fast and easy connectivity without the need for drivers or software.' The series' lowest price was $183.99, probably the 13.3-inch Plus DS variant. Use the record price for the Max DS.

unsourced: FOPO S11 / S7 / S1 / S10 cable count per screen and base M1/M2/M3 support. FOPO's product pages returned HTTP 429 to the fetcher every time, and storecheck returns only CSS for their descriptions. Our own without-drivers page quotes FOPO for the S11 ('one USB-C cable for both is not supported'), but I couldn't re-open FOPO's page to confirm it today.

FOPO S788 triple: whether one USB-C cable runs all three screens in UsbDisplay-driver mode, and the wattage of the included PD power supply. The page returned HTTP 429, and the manuals.plus PDF returned HTTP 403.
KYY X90E: KYY's own US product page saying whether the one-cable link is MST, and its macOS wording. I didn't open it, so the MST link is our labelled inference from TechRadar plus Plugable.
KYY X90E price today. TechRadar's $239.99 Amazon and $309.99 KYY-direct figures are from the review and aren't today's Black Friday price. Neither KYY's store nor Amazon was read today.

Power each extender draws over the laptop's USB-C port (watts per screen against the port's budget), so 'one cable' could be compared at full brightness. No maker page or reviewer I opened gave watts for the X90E or for any FOPO dual. The Duex Max DS 4.5 W figure appears only on our own page.
Xebec Tri-Screen 3 and ASUS ZenScreen MB16ACV one-cable conditions and today's prices. I didn't open either maker page within the call budget.
